chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abdullah ibn Sinan said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who advanced oil to another man on the condition that he take butter from him. He said, 'It is not valid.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on advancing oil in exchange for butter?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) invalidates a specific barter transaction where olive oil is advanced in exchange for a promise of butter, illustrating the principle of *Gharar* (uncertainty) or disparity in deferred exchanges of different commodities. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between permissible spot trades and invalid forward contracts involving heterogeneous goods, emphasizing the need for precise valuation and immediate possession to avoid riba-like elements.
